units.translation: 1091. And Pherecydes in the second book (3 F 10 J.) relates about Danae that Acrisius married Eurydice, daughter of Lacedaemon; and from them was born Danae. When he consulted the oracle about a male child, the god at Pytho prophesied that he himself would have no male child, but that from his daughter would be born one by whom he would be slain. He returned to Argos and made a bronze chamber underground in the courtyard of his house, where he placed Danae with a nurse; in this he guarded her, so that no child might be born from her. But Zeus fell in love with the girl, and flowed from the roof in the likeness of gold, and she received him in her lap; and Zeus revealed himself and had intercourse with the girl. From them was born Perseus, and Danae and the nurse reared him secretly, hiding him from Acrisius. When Perseus was three or four years old, Acrisius heard his voice as he played, and summoning Danae with the nurse through his servants, he killed the nurse, while Danae fled with the child to the altar of Zeus Herkeios.

Alone he asked her from whom the child had been born to her; and she said, 'From Zeus.' But he did not believe her, and placed her with the child in a chest, and closing it, cast it into the sea. And they were carried along and arrived at the island of Seriphos, and Dictys, son of Peristhenes, drew them out while fishing with a net. Then Danae begged him to open the chest, and he opened it and learned who they were, and brought them to his house and cared for them, as being his own kinsmen; for Dictys and Polydectes were sons of Androthoe, daughter of Castor, and Peristhenes, son of Damastor, son of Nauplius, son of Poseidon and Amymone, as Pherecydes says in the first book (3 F 4 J.).
